This table stores core attributes, such as dispute type, severity, status, and external references, while {@link shopping_mall_dispute_events}, {@link shopping_mall_dispute_parties}, and {@link shopping_mall_dispute_evidences} capture the detailed history and context.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key of the dispute.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Order primarily associated with this dispute, when the dispute is order-centric. {@link shopping_mall_orders}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_refund_request_id
foreignFields.description: Refund request that triggered or is central to this dispute, if applicable. {@link shopping_mall_refund_requests}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_payment_chargeback_id
foreignFields.description: Payment chargeback record associated with this dispute, when the dispute originates from a chargeback. {@link shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_risk_case_id
foreignFields.description: Risk case that tracks broader risk analysis related to this dispute. {@link shopping_mall_risk_cases}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_legal_hold_id
foreignFields.description: Legal hold that constrains modifications or deletions related to this dispute data. {@link shopping_mall_legal_holds}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin currently assigned as the owner or primary handler of this dispute. {@link shopping_mall_admins}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_case_sla_config_id
foreignFields.description: SLA configuration that governs this dispute, defining response or resolution targets. {@link shopping_mall_case_sla_configs}.

plainFields.name: dispute_code
plainFields.description: Business-visible identifier for the dispute case used across admin tools and communications.

plainFields.name: type
plainFields.description: High-level dispute type, such as payment_chargeback, refund_dispute, policy_violation, or other configured types.

plainFields.name: severity
plainFields.description: Business-defined severity level for prioritization, for example low, medium, high, or critical.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current lifecycle status of the dispute, such as open, under_investigation, resolved, or closed.

plainFields.name: summary
plainFields.description: Short human-readable summary describing the nature of the dispute for quick scanning in dashboards.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the dispute, used by admins to capture context and notes about the situation.

plainFields.name: opened_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the dispute was opened.

plainFields.name: resolved_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when a resolution decision was made for the dispute.

plainFields.name: closed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the dispute was fully closed and no further actions are expected.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this dispute record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this dispute record was last updated.

models.name: shopping_mall_dispute_parties
models.description:
Entities that participate in a dispute, such as customers, sellers, admins, or external entities.

This table links {@link shopping_mall_disputes} to the parties involved and classifies each party by role (for example complainant, respondent, or observer) and actor type. It supports multiple parties per dispute and multiple roles per actor when necessary.

The design keeps the schema normalized by storing only identifiers and role metadata without duplicating profile data from the underlying actor tables.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key of the dispute party.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_dispute_id
foreignFields.description: Dispute that this party is associated with. {@link shopping_mall_disputes}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer participating in the dispute, when actor_type is customer. {@link shopping_mall_customers}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller participating in the dispute, when actor_type is seller. {@link shopping_mall_sellers}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin participating in the dispute, when actor_type is admin. {@link shopping_mall_admins}.

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Type of party, such as customer, seller, admin, or external, used to interpret which foreign keys are populated.

plainFields.name: role
plainFields.description: Role of this party in the dispute, for example complainant, respondent, witness, or observer.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Name shown in admin tools for this party, which may be derived from the actor profile or manually entered for external parties.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this dispute party record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this dispute party record was last updated.

models.name: shopping_mall_dispute_events
models.description:
Timeline of events that occur during the lifecycle of a dispute.

Each record documents a single business event related to a {@link shopping_mall_disputes} instance, such as creation, assignment, evidence submission, note additions, escalation, or resolution. Events support detailed audit tracking, SLA analysis, and operational visibility.

This table is append-only, capturing immutable history without soft deletion to maintain integrity of the dispute timeline.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key of the dispute event.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_dispute_id
foreignFields.description: Dispute that this event relates to. {@link shopping_mall_disputes}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin who performed the action or recorded this event, when applicable. {@link shopping_mall_admins}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer involved in this event, when customer-initiated or customer-facing. {@link shopping_mall_customers}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller involved in this event, when seller-initiated or seller-facing. {@link shopping_mall_sellers}.

plainFields.name: event_type
plainFields.description: Type of event, such as created, note_added, status_changed, escalated, evidence_added, or external_update.

plainFields.name: status_before
plainFields.description: Dispute status before this event occurred, when the event changed the status.

plainFields.name: status_after
plainFields.description: Dispute status after this event occurred, when the event changed the status.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-readable description or notes for this event, explaining what happened or why.

plainFields.name: occurred_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this event occurred in business terms.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this dispute event record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this dispute event record was last updated.

models.name: shopping_mall_dispute_evidences
models.description:
Evidence artifacts attached to disputes to support investigations and decisions.

Stores references to documents, images, messages, or external systems that are relevant to a {@link shopping_mall_disputes} instance. Evidence items may optionally be linked to a specific {@link shopping_mall_dispute_events} entry that introduced them.

Only metadata and URIs are stored here; the actual binary content is expected to live in separate storage services. Records are append-only to preserve evidentiary integrity.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key of the dispute evidence.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_dispute_id
foreignFields.description: Dispute that this evidence supports. {@link shopping_mall_disputes}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_dispute_event_id
foreignFields.description: Specific dispute event that introduced this evidence, when applicable. {@link shopping_mall_dispute_events}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin who attached this evidence, when the evidence was supplied by an admin. {@link shopping_mall_admins}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who provided this evidence, when relevant. {@link shopping_mall_customers}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller who provided this evidence, when relevant. {@link shopping_mall_sellers}.

plainFields.name: evidence_type
plainFields.description: Type of evidence, such as image, document, message_log, or external_reference.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Short title or label that describes this evidence item in admin tools.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description or notes about what this evidence shows or why it is relevant.

plainFields.name: uri
plainFields.description: URI pointing to the stored evidence content in external storage or another system.

plainFields.name: checksum
plainFields.description: Optional checksum or hash of the evidence content for integrity verification.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this dispute evidence record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this dispute evidence record was last updated.

models.name: shopping_mall_case_sla_configs
models.description:
Configuration of service-level agreements (SLAs) for different case types such as cancellations, refunds, and disputes.

Defines time-bound expectations for response or resolution by actor role and case type, for example seller must respond within X hours to a refund request. These configs are referenced by {@link shopping_mall_cancellation_requests}, {@link shopping_mall_refund_requests}, and {@link shopping_mall_disputes}.

This table allows policy teams to adjust SLA thresholds without changing core business tables, and it is treated as a primary configuration entity in the refunds and disputes domain.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key of the case SLA configuration.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_business_policy_version_id
foreignFields.description: Business policy version this SLA config is associated with, enabling policy evolution tracking. {@link shopping_mall_policy_versions}.

plainFields.name: case_type
plainFields.description: Type of case this SLA applies to, such as cancellation, refund, or dispute.

plainFields.name: actor_role
plainFields.description: Actor role whose behavior is constrained, such as customer, seller, or admin.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Action governed by the SLA, for example initial_response or final_decision.

plainFields.name: target_duration_seconds
plainFields.description: Target time window in seconds within which the action should be completed from the relevant start time.

plainFields.name: warning_duration_seconds
plainFields.description: Optional duration in seconds after which a warning should be raised before the SLA breach occurs.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Flag indicating whether this SLA rule is currently active for new cases.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this SLA configuration record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this SLA configuration record was last updated.

models.name: shopping_mall_case_sla_violations
models.description:
Recorded SLA breaches for specific cases such as cancellations, refunds, or disputes.

Each row represents a detected violation of a particular {@link shopping_mall_case_sla_configs} rule, linking back to the concrete business case. These records provide an immutable audit of SLA performance, enabling compliance reporting and operational tuning.

The table is subsidiary because it supports analysis and risk management rather than representing a primary business case itself.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key of the case SLA violation.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_case_sla_config_id
foreignFields.description: SLA configuration that was violated. {@link shopping_mall_case_sla_configs}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_cancellation_request_id
foreignFields.description: Cancellation request that violated this SLA, when the case is a cancellation. {@link shopping_mall_cancellation_requests}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_refund_request_id
foreignFields.description: Refund request that violated this SLA, when the case is a refund. {@link shopping_mall_refund_requests}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_dispute_id
foreignFields.description: Dispute that violated this SLA, when the case is a dispute. {@link shopping_mall_disputes}.

plainFields.name: case_type
plainFields.description: Type of case that violated the SLA, such as cancellation, refund, or dispute, mirroring the SLA config.

plainFields.name: actor_role
plainFields.description: Actor role responsible for satisfying the SLA, such as seller or admin.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Action for which the SLA was defined, such as initial_response or final_decision.

plainFields.name: breach_duration_seconds
plainFields.description: Number of seconds by which the SLA was exceeded beyond the target duration.

plainFields.name: detected_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the system detected the SLA violation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this SLA violation record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this SLA violation record was last updated.

models.name: shopping_mall_reviews
models.description:
Customer-written product reviews and ratings.

Stores the canonical current version of each public review that a customer has written about a purchased product or SKU. Each review is linked to a specific order item to ensure verified purchase semantics and to a product and optional SKU for aggregation. The table captures rating score, optional title and body, visibility and moderation states, and flags such as verified purchase and incentivized review.

The historical versions of the content are tracked in {@link shopping_mall_review_versions}. Reports and moderation actions referencing a review are stored in {@link shopping_mall_review_reports} and {@link shopping_mall_review_moderation_actions}. Helpful votes are stored in {@link shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes}.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Unique identifier for the review.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who authored the review. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_id
foreignFields.description: Reviewed product. {@link shopping_mall_products.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_sku_id
foreignFields.description: Reviewed SKU variant when the review targets a specific SKU. Nullable when the review is at product level only. {@link shopping_mall_skus.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Order item that granted eligibility for this review. Nullable when the review is not tied to a single order item (for example legacy imports). {@link shopping_mall_order_items.id}.

plainFields.name: rating
plainFields.description: Star rating value given by the customer. Uses a discrete integer scale such as 1–5 where higher numbers represent more positive evaluations.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Optional short title summarizing the review. Used for quick scanning in lists.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Optional free-form text body containing the detailed review content provided by the customer.

plainFields.name: visibility_status
plainFields.description: Current visibility status of the review in customer-facing contexts. Typical values include visible, hidden, pending_moderation, and removed. Business logic controls which values are allowed.

plainFields.name: moderation_state
plainFields.description: High-level moderation state reflecting whether the review has passed checks, is flagged, or is under investigation. Used to drive moderation queues and workflows.

plainFields.name: verified_purchase
plainFields.description: Indicates whether this review is considered a verified purchase based on linkage to completed order items and business rules.

plainFields.name: incentivized
plainFields.description: Indicates whether the review was written under some incentive program, such as coupons or rewards. Required for transparency and compliance with regulations.

plainFields.name: helpfulness_score
plainFields.description: Derived integer score representing net helpfulness (for example helpful minus not helpful votes). Updated by application logic for ranking but not used as the authoritative vote log.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the review was first created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the review was last updated, either by the author or by system processes such as moderation state changes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. When not null the review should be excluded from normal user-facing queries but retained for audit.

models.name: shopping_mall_review_versions
models.description:
Historical versions of review content for audit and change tracking.

Each row captures a point-in-time snapshot of the content and key flags of a review from {@link shopping_mall_reviews}. Versions are append-only and allow the platform to reconstruct how a review looked at any time, including rating, title, body, visibility status, and moderation state.

Snapshots are typically created whenever a customer edits their review or when moderation actions change visibility-critical fields. This table supports audit, dispute resolution, and compliance investigations.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Unique identifier for the review version snapshot.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_review_id
foreignFields.description: The review whose state is captured in this version snapshot. {@link shopping_mall_reviews.id}.

plainFields.name: rating
plainFields.description: Rating value at the time of this snapshot. Preserves the historical score even if the customer later edits it.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Review title at the time of this snapshot. May differ from the current review title.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Review body text at the time of this snapshot. Captures the exact wording used for audit purposes.

plainFields.name: visibility_status
plainFields.description: Visibility status of the review at the time of this snapshot. Allows reconstruction of when the review was visible or hidden.

plainFields.name: moderation_state
plainFields.description: Moderation state at the time of this snapshot. Used for investigating moderation decisions and their timeline.

plainFields.name: verified_purchase
plainFields.description: Whether the review was marked as a verified purchase at the time of this snapshot.

plainFields.name: incentivized
plainFields.description: Whether the review was flagged as incentivized at the time of this snapshot.

plainFields.name: snapshot_reason
plainFields.description: Optional business-level reason describing why this snapshot was taken, such as author_edit, moderation_change, or system_migration.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this version snapshot was created. Represents the effective time of the captured state.

models.name: shopping_mall_review_reports
models.description:
Reports and flags submitted against reviews.

Represents complaints and reports created by customers, sellers, or internal systems regarding potentially problematic reviews stored in {@link shopping_mall_reviews}. Each report records who reported, the category of the issue, free-form details, and current processing state.

Reports feed moderation workflows and can be linked to moderation actions in {@link shopping_mall_review_moderation_actions}. Multiple reports may exist for a single review, and a single reporter may file reports on multiple reviews over time.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Unique identifier for the review report.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_review_id
foreignFields.description: The review that has been reported as problematic. {@link shopping_mall_reviews.id}.

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Type of actor that submitted the report, such as customer, seller, or system. Used to interpret reporter context in higher layers.

plainFields.name: reporter_actor_reference
plainFields.description: Opaque reference identifier for the reporter, interpreted according to actor_type by the application layer. Not enforced as a foreign key to avoid polymorphic nullable FKs in this component.

plainFields.name: reason_code
plainFields.description: Categorized reason for the report, such as offensive_content, spam, conflict_of_interest, or other. Used to group and prioritize moderation work.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional free-form description provided by the reporter, giving more context about why the review is considered problematic.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Processing status of the report, such as open, under_review, resolved, or dismissed. Drives moderation queues and SLAs.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the report was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the report record was last updated, for example when status changes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for the report. When set, the report is excluded from normal moderation views but retained for audit.

models.name: shopping_mall_review_moderation_actions
models.description:
Moderation decisions and actions applied to reviews and related reports.

Records discrete actions taken by admins or automated policies when handling reported or flagged reviews. Examples include hiding a review, restoring a review, editing visibility status, or applying sanctions to authors.

Each row links to the affected review in {@link shopping_mall_reviews}, optionally to a specific report in {@link shopping_mall_review_reports}, and to the admin who performed the action from {@link shopping_mall_admins}. Actions are append-only and provide a full audit trail for governance and compliance.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Unique identifier for the moderation action.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_review_id
foreignFields.description: Review that the moderation action targets. {@link shopping_mall_reviews.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_review_report_id
foreignFields.description: Optional associated report that triggered this moderation action. Nullable because some actions may be proactive or system-driven without a specific report. {@link shopping_mall_review_reports.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin who performed the moderation action, when not automated. Nullable for system-generated actions. {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of moderation action performed, such as hide_review, restore_review, edit_visibility, or escalate_dispute.

plainFields.name: previous_visibility_status
plainFields.description: Previous visibility status of the review before this action, when relevant. Useful for debugging and audit but may be null when not applicable.

plainFields.name: new_visibility_status
plainFields.description: New visibility status applied by this action, when the action changes visibility. Null when the action does not affect visibility.

plainFields.name: previous_moderation_state
plainFields.description: Previous moderation state before this action, when relevant.

plainFields.name: new_moderation_state
plainFields.description: New moderation state applied by this action, when relevant.

plainFields.name: reason_code
plainFields.description: Categorized reason for the moderation action, for example policy_violation, legal_request, or manual_override.

plainFields.name: note
plainFields.description: Optional internal note providing additional context or explanation for the moderation decision.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderation action was recorded.

models.name: shopping_mall_review_helpful_votes
models.description:
Helpful vote records on reviews by customers.

Represents the many-to-many relationship between customers and reviews where customers indicate whether a review is helpful. Each row corresponds to one customer’s vote on one review.

This table is the authoritative log of votes used to derive aggregated helpfulness metrics in {@link shopping_mall_reviews}. It supports both positive and negative votes so that net helpfulness can be computed.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Unique identifier for the helpful vote entry.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_review_id
foreignFields.description: Review that received the helpfulness vote. {@link shopping_mall_reviews.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who cast the helpfulness vote. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: is_helpful
plainFields.description: Indicates whether the customer marked the review as helpful (true) or not helpful (false).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the vote was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the vote was last updated, for example when a customer changes from helpful to not helpful.

models.name: shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates
models.description:
Precomputed rating aggregates per product.

Stores summary statistics such as average rating and review counts for each product, derived from the underlying reviews in {@link shopping_mall_reviews}. This table is optimized for fast reads from product detail and listing pages.

The table is maintained by batch jobs or triggers outside of this schema and should be treated as a materialized aggregate view rather than a source of truth for individual reviews.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Unique identifier for the product rating aggregate row.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_id
foreignFields.description: Product whose rating metrics are aggregated in this row. {@link shopping_mall_products.id}.

plainFields.name: average_rating
plainFields.description: Average rating value for the product computed from included reviews. Nullable when no reviews exist.

plainFields.name: rating_count
plainFields.description: Total number of included reviews contributing to the aggregate metrics for this product.

plainFields.name: rating_1_count
plainFields.description: Number of included reviews with the lowest rating value, for example 1-star reviews.

plainFields.name: rating_2_count
plainFields.description: Number of included reviews with the second rating value on the scale, for example 2-star reviews.

plainFields.name: rating_3_count
plainFields.description: Number of included reviews with a mid-range rating value, for example 3-star reviews.

plainFields.name: rating_4_count
plainFields.description: Number of included reviews with a high rating value, for example 4-star reviews.

plainFields.name: rating_5_count
plainFields.description: Number of included reviews with the highest rating value, for example 5-star reviews.

plainFields.name: last_computed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the aggregate metrics were last recomputed for this product.

models.name: shopping_mall_sku_rating_aggregates
models.description:
Precomputed rating aggregates per SKU variant.

Stores summary statistics such as average rating and review counts for each SKU, derived from the underlying reviews in {@link shopping_mall_reviews} that are associated with specific SKUs. This enables variant-level quality signals and filtering.

The table is maintained by background processes and is conceptually a materialized aggregate view. It should not be manually edited as part of normal business workflows.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Unique identifier for the SKU rating aggregate row.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_sku_id
foreignFields.description: SKU whose rating metrics are aggregated in this row. {@link shopping_mall_skus.id}.

plainFields.name: average_rating
plainFields.description: Average rating value for the SKU computed from included reviews. Nullable when no reviews exist for this SKU.

plainFields.name: rating_count
plainFields.description: Total number of included reviews that target this SKU and contribute to the aggregate metrics.

plainFields.name: rating_1_count
plainFields.description: Number of included reviews for this SKU with the lowest rating value, for example 1-star reviews.

plainFields.name: rating_2_count
plainFields.description: Number of included reviews for this SKU with the second rating value on the scale, for example 2-star reviews.

plainFields.name: rating_3_count
plainFields.description: Number of included reviews for this SKU with a mid-range rating value, for example 3-star reviews.

plainFields.name: rating_4_count
plainFields.description: Number of included reviews for this SKU with a high rating value, for example 4-star reviews.

plainFields.name: rating_5_count
plainFields.description: Number of included reviews for this SKU with the highest rating value, for example 5-star reviews.

plainFields.name: last_computed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the aggregate metrics were last recomputed for this SKU.

models.name: shopping_mall_review_eligibilities
models.description:
Eligibility records indicating when customers are allowed to write reviews.

Represents the link between delivered order items and the customer’s permission to submit a review for a product or SKU. Each row indicates that a specific customer became eligible to review a specific product or SKU based on an order item reaching a completed or delivered state.

The table captures eligibility status, timing constraints such as expiration, and whether the eligibility has already been consumed by an actual review in {@link shopping_mall_reviews}. This supports business rules like one review per purchase, review windows, and verified purchase checks.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Unique identifier for the review eligibility record.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who becomes eligible to write a review. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Order item whose completion or delivery created this review eligibility. {@link shopping_mall_order_items.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_id
foreignFields.description: Product that may be reviewed under this eligibility. {@link shopping_mall_products.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_sku_id
foreignFields.description: SKU variant that may be reviewed under this eligibility when the purchase was for a specific variant. Nullable when the eligibility is only at product level. {@link shopping_mall_skus.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_review_id
foreignFields.description: Review that consumed this eligibility, when one has been created. Nullable when the eligibility has not yet been used. {@link shopping_mall_reviews.id}.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current eligibility status, such as eligible, used, expired, or revoked. Controls whether the customer can currently create a review from this record.

plainFields.name: eligible_from
plainFields.description: Timestamp from which the customer is allowed to submit a review based on this eligibility, typically when the order item is marked delivered or completed.

plainFields.name: eligible_until
plainFields.description: Optional timestamp after which this eligibility expires and can no longer be used to create a new review.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the eligibility record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the eligibility record was last updated, for example when status changes.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_warehouses
models.description:
Physical or logical warehouses owned by sellers for inventory storage and shipment origin.

Each warehouse belongs to exactly one seller and represents a location from which SKUs are stocked and fulfilled. The warehouse stores high-level metadata such as internal code, human-readable name, operational status, and whether it is the default origin for the seller.

Address details are normalized into {@link shopping_mall_seller_warehouse_addresses} so that postal information remains independent and auditable over time. Inventory adjustment records in {@link shopping_mall_inventory_adjustments} reference warehouses to indicate where stock changes occurred.

Admins may read and govern warehouses across sellers, while sellers typically manage only their own warehouses via seller-portal flows.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Unique identifier of the seller warehouse.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller that owns this warehouse. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Seller-scoped warehouse code used for internal reference. Must be unique per seller and stable once assigned for reconciliation.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Human-readable warehouse name shown in seller portal and internal tools.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional longer description of the warehouse, such as notes about purpose, capacity, or internal comments.

plainFields.name: is_default_origin
plainFields.description: Whether this warehouse is the seller’s default shipping origin for new SKUs and orders when no explicit origin is chosen.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Operational status of the warehouse from business perspective, e.g. active, inactive, suspended. Controls whether it can be used for new fulfilment operations.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the warehouse record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the warehouse record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. When set, the warehouse is logically removed from new operations but preserved for historical reference.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_warehouse_addresses
models.description:
Postal and contact address details attached to seller warehouses.

This table stores normalized address information for {@link shopping_mall_seller_warehouses}. Using a separate table avoids repeating address columns across warehouse-like entities and supports future extension such as multiple address types per warehouse (shipping origin, return address) while maintaining 3NF.

Warehouse address records are typically managed indirectly via seller-portal flows that edit a warehouse together with its address fields rather than through independent CRUD operations.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Unique identifier of the warehouse address row.

foreignFields.name: seller_warehouse_id
foreignFields.description: Warehouse that this address belongs to. One-to-one relationship with {@link shopping_mall_seller_warehouses.id}.

foreignFields.name: country_id
foreignFields.description: Country of the warehouse location. {@link shopping_mall_countries.id}.

foreignFields.name: region_id
foreignFields.description: Optional region or state of the warehouse address. {@link shopping_mall_regions.id}.

plainFields.name: recipient_name
plainFields.description: Recipient or contact name used for carrier labels and operational communication.

plainFields.name: line1
plainFields.description: First line of the warehouse street address (street, number, or primary descriptor).

plainFields.name: line2
plainFields.description: Second address line, such as building, floor, or suite information.

plainFields.name: city
plainFields.description: City or locality of the warehouse.

plainFields.name: postal_code
plainFields.description: Postal or ZIP code of the warehouse location, following local formatting rules.

plainFields.name: phone
plainFields.description: Optional phone number for the warehouse to be shared with carriers and used for delivery issues.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this address record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this address record was last updated.

models.name: shopping_mall_inventory_adjustment_reasons
models.description:
Master data representing standardized reasons for inventory adjustments.

Each row describes a business-level reason why stock is increased or decreased, such as purchase, correction, damage, shrinkage, or manual reconciliation. These reasons are referenced by inventory adjustment records in {@link shopping_mall_inventory_adjustments}.

Having a dedicated reasons table ensures consistent semantics across sellers and time and supports governance, reporting, and policy enforcement by admins.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Unique identifier of the inventory adjustment reason.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Stable, system-wide reason code, for example PURCHASE_INBOUND or STOCK_CORRECTION. Used in configuration and reporting.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Human-readable name of the adjustment reason shown in UI and reports.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional detailed explanation of when this reason should be used and any relevant policy notes.

plainFields.name: direction
plainFields.description: Business direction of the adjustment for reporting, such as increase, decrease, or neutral. Application logic interprets this string as an enum.

plainFields.name: is_system_managed
plainFields.description: Indicates whether this reason is system-managed and cannot be edited or deleted by regular admins.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the reason record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the reason record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. When set, the reason is no longer available for new adjustments but remains for historical records.

models.name: shopping_mall_inventory_adjustments
models.description:
Atomic inventory adjustment events per seller, SKU, and warehouse.

Each record represents a single change to the on-hand or available quantity of a SKU for a seller at a given warehouse. Adjustments are used for manual corrections, inbound receipts, write-offs, damage, shrinkage, and other non-order-based changes.

The table links to {@link shopping_mall_sellers} for ownership, {@link shopping_mall_skus} for the affected SKU, {@link shopping_mall_seller_warehouses} for the physical location, and {@link shopping_mall_inventory_adjustment_reasons} for the standardized reason. Optional references to sessions and admins allow clear audit trails about who initiated the adjustment.

This table is append-only from a business perspective; corrections are expressed as compensating adjustments rather than in-place updates, maintaining a robust audit history aligned with risk and compliance expectations.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Unique identifier of the inventory adjustment event.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller that owns the stock being adjusted. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

foreignFields.name: sku_id
foreignFields.description: SKU whose inventory is adjusted. {@link shopping_mall_skus.id}.

foreignFields.name: seller_warehouse_id
foreignFields.description: Warehouse where the stock change occurs. {@link shopping_mall_seller_warehouses.id}.

foreignFields.name: inventory_adjustment_reason_id
foreignFields.description: Reason category explaining why this adjustment was performed. {@link shopping_mall_inventory_adjustment_reasons.id}.

foreignFields.name: seller_session_id
foreignFields.description: Optional seller session that initiated the adjustment, for traceability. {@link shopping_mall_seller_sessions.id}.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: Optional admin responsible for this adjustment when done via admin tools. {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

foreignFields.name: admin_session_id
foreignFields.description: Optional admin session associated with the adjustment event. {@link shopping_mall_admin_sessions.id}.

plainFields.name: direction
plainFields.description: Adjustment direction from the event’s own perspective, for example increase or decrease. Typically matches or refines the direction on the reason.

plainFields.name: quantity_delta
plainFields.description: Quantity change applied to the SKU at this warehouse. Positive values increase stock, negative values decrease stock.

plainFields.name: reference_type
plainFields.description: Optional business reference type string describing the origin context, e.g. inbound_shipment, inventory_audit, manual_correction.

plainFields.name: reference_id
plainFields.description: Optional external business identifier associated with the adjustment, such as an internal document ID or shipment reference.

plainFields.name: note
plainFields.description: Optional free-text note describing details of the adjustment for human audit and explanation.

plainFields.name: occurred_at
plainFields.description: Business timestamp when the stock change actually occurred, which may differ slightly from record creation time.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this adjustment record was inserted.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when metadata of this adjustment record was last updated. Quantity and core links are typically immutable.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_order_metrics_snapshots
models.description:
Time-series snapshots of seller order-related metrics for analytics and monitoring.

Each record represents aggregated metrics for a seller over a specific snapshot period, such as a day. The table captures values like order counts, GMV, cancellation volume, refund volume, and derived KPIs used for dashboards and risk checks.

Snapshots are computed from transactional sources such as {@link shopping_mall_orders}, {@link shopping_mall_order_items}, and refund components, but those details are not duplicated here beyond raw metrics. This table is treated as an append-only snapshot store with a clear snapshot_date dimension to support efficient trend queries and KPI computations.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Unique identifier of the seller order metrics snapshot row.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller for whom these order metrics are recorded. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: snapshot_date
plainFields.description: Date or date-time representing the logical period boundary for this snapshot, typically the start of the day being summarized.

plainFields.name: timezone
plainFields.description: Business timezone identifier used when aggregating metrics, such as Asia/Seoul. Ensures consistent day boundaries across reports.

plainFields.name: orders_placed_count
plainFields.description: Number of orders that entered a placed or confirmed state for the seller within the snapshot period.

plainFields.name: orders_paid_count
plainFields.description: Number of orders that reached a paid state for the seller within the snapshot period.

plainFields.name: orders_cancelled_count
plainFields.description: Number of orders or order segments cancelled for the seller during the snapshot period, regardless of reason.

plainFields.name: orders_refunded_count
plainFields.description: Number of orders or line segments with approved refunds affecting the seller during the snapshot period.

plainFields.name: gmv_amount
plainFields.description: Gross merchandise value for the seller’s orders in the snapshot period, before cancellations and refunds.

plainFields.name: nmv_amount
plainFields.description: Net merchandise value after accounting for cancellations and refunds in the snapshot period, from the seller’s perspective.

plainFields.name: shipping_fee_amount
plainFields.description: Total shipping fees charged to customers associated with the seller’s items in the snapshot period.

plainFields.name: refund_amount
plainFields.description: Total customer refund amount impacting the seller’s items in the snapshot period.

plainFields.name: chargeback_amount
plainFields.description: Total amount involved in chargebacks associated with the seller in the snapshot period.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot row was created by the metrics computation process.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot row was last recalculated or corrected, if applicable.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_performance_snapshots
models.description:
Aggregated performance KPIs per seller at defined points in time.

This table summarizes seller-level health indicators such as refund rates, cancellation rates, late shipment rates, dispute counts, and rating statistics. It is used by admins and risk engines to classify sellers into tiers and to trigger governance workflows.

The data is derived from transactional tables like orders, shipments, refunds, disputes, and reviews ({@link shopping_mall_orders}, {@link shopping_mall_shipments}, {@link shopping_mall_reviews}), but those details are not repeated here. Instead, this table stores normalized numeric metrics in snapshot form, supporting trend analysis and segmentation while preserving 3NF in the transactional schema.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Unique identifier of the seller performance snapshot row.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller whose performance metrics are represented. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: snapshot_date
plainFields.description: Logical date or date-time representing when this performance snapshot was computed.

plainFields.name: timezone
plainFields.description: Timezone context used for computing the performance window, such as Asia/Seoul.

plainFields.name: order_defect_rate
plainFields.description: Order defect rate for the seller during the analysis window, expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

plainFields.name: refund_rate
plainFields.description: Refund rate for the seller during the analysis window, expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

plainFields.name: cancellation_rate
plainFields.description: Cancellation rate for the seller during the analysis window, expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

plainFields.name: late_shipment_rate
plainFields.description: Proportion of shipments that were dispatched or delivered late in the analysis window, expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

plainFields.name: chargeback_rate
plainFields.description: Proportion of paid orders that resulted in chargebacks during the analysis window, expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

plainFields.name: average_rating
plainFields.description: Average product rating (for example 1–5 scale) for the seller’s catalog at this snapshot point, derived from reviews.

plainFields.name: rating_count
plainFields.description: Number of ratings considered when computing average_rating.

plainFields.name: dispute_open_count
plainFields.description: Number of open disputes involving the seller at the time of snapshot computation.

plainFields.name: tier
plainFields.description: Optional seller tier classification at this snapshot (for example new, standard, premium, high_risk). Evaluated by business rules.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the snapshot row was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the snapshot row was last updated due to recomputation or corrections.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_subscription_plans
models.description:
Catalog of subscription plans and service offerings available to sellers.

Each row describes a plan that a seller can subscribe to, such as basic, standard, or premium tiers. Plans define attributes like billing period, base fee, included features, and whether they are currently available for new sign-ups.

Subscriptions in {@link shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions} reference these plans to determine pricing and entitlements. Admins manage this table to add, modify, or retire plans over time while preserving historical understanding of what each plan contained when a subscription was active.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Unique identifier of the seller subscription plan.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Stable business code for the plan, such as BASIC, PRO, or ENTERPRISE. Used in configuration, integrations, and reporting.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Human-readable plan name exposed to sellers in the portal.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional detailed description of features and benefits included in this plan.

plainFields.name: billing_period
plainFields.description: Billing period identifier, for example monthly or yearly. Application logic treats this string as an enum.

plainFields.name: currency
plainFields.description: ISO currency code used for billing this plan, such as USD or KRW.

plainFields.name: price_amount
plainFields.description: Subscription fee amount per billing period, expressed in the plan’s currency.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Whether the plan is currently active and available for new subscriptions. Existing subscriptions may continue even if the plan is deactivated.

plainFields.name: effective_from
plainFields.description: Timestamp from which the plan is considered effective for new subscriptions and pricing calculations.

plainFields.name: effective_until
plainFields.description: Optional timestamp after which the plan is no longer offered for new subscriptions. Null means open-ended.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the plan record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the plan record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for plans that should no longer appear anywhere, subject to business retention rules.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_subscriptions
models.description:
Individual subscriptions of sellers to specific subscription plans.

Each record links a seller to a plan from {@link shopping_mall_seller_subscription_plans} and tracks the subscription lifecycle, including start and end timestamps, current status, and billing amounts.

These records are used to determine which features and limits apply to a seller at a given time and to drive billing, invoicing, and revenue recognition logic. They align with the business model requirements for seller subscriptions and service fees outlined in the revenue and goals specification.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Unique identifier for the seller subscription instance.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller who owns this subscription. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

foreignFields.name: seller_subscription_plan_id
foreignFields.description: Subscription plan that defines pricing and entitlements for this subscription. {@link shopping_mall_seller_subscription_plans.id}.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current subscription status, such as pending, active, past_due, cancelled, or expired. Application logic treats this as a business enum.

plainFields.name: started_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the subscription became active for the seller.

plainFields.name: ended_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the subscription ended or is scheduled to end. Null while the subscription is ongoing.

plainFields.name: next_billing_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the next expected billing event, if applicable for this subscription.

plainFields.name: currency
plainFields.description: Currency code in which this subscription is billed. Usually matches the plan currency but stored explicitly for historical accuracy.

plainFields.name: price_amount
plainFields.description: Nominal price per billing period for this subscription at the time of activation, in the subscription currency.

plainFields.name: discount_amount
plainFields.description: Per-period discount amount applied to this subscription, if any. Zero means no discount.

plainFields.name: metadata_json
plainFields.description: Optional JSON-encoded metadata capturing configuration or context specific to this subscription instance. Not used for computed values.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the subscription record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the subscription record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. Used when a subscription is logically removed from normal views but retained for compliance and revenue audits.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_fee_charges
models.description:
Individual fee and commission charges applied to sellers for transactional and service events.

Each record represents a distinct charge that impacts the net earnings or balance of a seller, such as transaction commissions, platform-owned fees, subscription charges, advertising fees, adjustments, or penalties.

The table links to {@link shopping_mall_sellers} and may optionally reference an order in {@link shopping_mall_orders}, a refund in {@link shopping_mall_payment_refunds}, or a payout item in {@link shopping_mall_seller_payout_items} for reconciliation. It aligns with the revenue model by making each charge explicit, auditable, and traceable through time without pre-aggregating data.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Unique identifier of the seller fee charge row.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller to whom this fee charge applies. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: Optional related order that caused this charge, if any. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}.

foreignFields.name: payment_refund_id
foreignFields.description: Optional related payment refund record when this fee is associated with a refund event. {@link shopping_mall_payment_refunds.id}.

foreignFields.name: seller_payout_item_id
foreignFields.description: Optional payout item that settled this fee charge, used for reconciliation. {@link shopping_mall_seller_payout_items.id}.

plainFields.name: fee_type
plainFields.description: Business category of the fee, such as transaction_commission, platform_service_fee, subscription_fee, advertising_fee, or adjustment. Application treats this as an enum.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional human-readable description explaining the origin of the fee charge.

plainFields.name: currency
plainFields.description: Currency code in which the fee amount is expressed.

plainFields.name: amount
plainFields.description: Fee amount applied to the seller. Positive values represent charges to the seller (reducing net earnings), while negative values may represent fee reversals or credits.

plainFields.name: tax_amount
plainFields.description: Tax portion associated with this fee, if applicable, expressed in the same currency. Zero when no tax applies.

plainFields.name: is_platform_revenue
plainFields.description: Indicates whether this fee contributes to platform revenue (true) or is a pass-through amount due entirely to third parties (false).

plainFields.name: effective_date
plainFields.description: Business date on which the fee is considered effective for revenue recognition and reporting.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this fee charge record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this fee charge record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for logically removed fee charges, preserved for audit and reconciliation use cases.

models.name: shopping_mall_admin_roles
models.description:
Administrative role definitions for RBAC within the shoppingMall platform.

Each record represents a named role that can be assigned to one or more admin accounts. Roles encapsulate collections of permissions in application logic and are used to control which governance and operational actions each admin may perform.

Roles are referenced from {@link shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments} and may be used implicitly in audit log interpretations and risk workflows.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the admin role record.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Stable, unique machine-oriented code for the role (for example, "super_admin", "operations_admin"). Used in configuration and application logic.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Human-readable display name for the role as shown in admin tools.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional detailed description explaining the purpose, scope, and intended users of this role.

plainFields.name: is_system
plainFields.description: Indicates whether this role is a system-protected role that cannot be freely edited or deleted by regular admins.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this role was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this role was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. When set, the role should no longer be assigned to admins but remains for historical reference.

models.name: shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments
models.description:
Assignments linking admin accounts to administrative roles.

Each record associates a specific admin with a specific {@link shopping_mall_admin_roles} entry and indicates when and why the assignment was made. This table forms the many-to-many junction between admins and roles and is critical for RBAC evaluation.

Assignments may be soft-deleted when revoked, but historical admin audit logs reference them indirectly through the roles and permissions granted at the time of an action.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the admin role assignment record.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Identifier of the admin account receiving the role assignment. {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_admin_role_id
foreignFields.description: Identifier of the role assigned to the admin. {@link shopping_mall_admin_roles.id}.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Optional human-readable reason or justification for granting this role to the admin.

plainFields.name: granted_by_admin_id
plainFields.description: Identifier of the admin who granted this role. Nullable for system-granted roles. References {@link shopping_mall_admins.id} logically, but kept as a plain field for flexibility in historical data.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this role assignment was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this role assignment was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp indicating when the role was revoked for this admin.

models.name: shopping_mall_admin_permissions
models.description:
Catalog of fine-grained administrative permissions used by RBAC.

Each record describes a single permission that can be conceptually linked to roles or directly evaluated by application logic. Permissions typically correspond to actions such as viewing or editing users, moderating catalog entries, or resolving disputes.

Although there is no explicit role-permission join table in this component, permission codes are referenced in configuration and in {@link shopping_mall_business_policies} for governance rules.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the admin permission record.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Stable, unique machine-oriented code for the permission (for example, "user.manage", "seller.suspend"). Used in RBAC evaluation.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Human-readable display name for the permission as seen by admins configuring RBAC.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional detailed description of what the permission allows and any constraints or warnings.

plainFields.name: category
plainFields.description: Optional high-level category or module name to group related permissions (for example, "users", "orders", "catalog").

plainFields.name: is_system
plainFields.description: Indicates whether this permission is system-defined and cannot be removed or arbitrarily modified.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this permission definition was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this permission definition was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. When set, the permission is no longer assignable but kept for historical interpretation of past actions.

models.name: shopping_mall_admin_audit_logs
models.description:
Append-only audit trail of administrative actions performed on the shoppingMall platform.

Each record represents a single action taken by an admin or system process against some business entity, including changes to users, sellers, catalog, orders, refunds, disputes, policies, or configuration.

The table supports compliance, forensic analysis, and governance reporting and is typically queried by time range, admin, entity type, or action type. Records are never soft-deleted or updated once created.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the admin audit log entry.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Identifier of the admin who performed the action. Nullable for system-initiated events. {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Machine-readable code identifying the type of action performed (for example, "USER_STATUS_CHANGE", "SELLER_APPROVAL", "PRODUCT_BLOCK").

plainFields.name: entity_type
plainFields.description: Type of business entity affected by the action (for example, "customer", "seller", "product", "order", "refund_request", "dispute").

plainFields.name: entity_id
plainFields.description: Identifier of the target entity as stored in its domain table. Nullable for actions that do not target a specific entity.

plainFields.name: entity_display
plainFields.description: Human-friendly identifier for the target entity such as email, seller name, or order code, captured at the time of the action.

plainFields.name: request_id
plainFields.description: Optional correlation identifier for the request or session in which the action occurred, useful for tracing grouped operations.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: Best-effort textual representation of the remote IP address from which the admin action was triggered.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: User agent string or descriptive label for the client used to perform the action.

plainFields.name: message
plainFields.description: Short human-readable summary of the action, suitable for audit browsing and search.

plainFields.name: before_snapshot
plainFields.description: Optional serialized representation of relevant entity fields before the change, stored as text for audit purposes.

plainFields.name: after_snapshot
plainFields.description: Optional serialized representation of relevant entity fields after the change, stored as text for audit purposes.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this audit log entry was recorded.

models.name: shopping_mall_legal_holds
models.description:
Legal hold records that prevent deletion or alteration of data for compliance or investigation.

Each legal hold is created by an admin to preserve information related to specific users, sellers, orders, disputes, or other entities for legal or regulatory reasons. Holds have a lifecycle from creation through possible release.

Targets of a legal hold are represented in {@link shopping_mall_legal_hold_targets}, allowing a single hold to apply to many business entities across domains.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the legal hold record.

foreignFields.name: created_by_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Identifier of the admin who created the legal hold. {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

foreignFields.name: released_by_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Identifier of the admin who formally released the legal hold, if any. {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Stable identifier or reference code for the legal hold, suitable for external correspondence and internal search.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Short human-readable title describing the legal hold, such as a case name or subject summary.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional detailed explanation of the reason for the legal hold, including legal context and scope notes.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the legal hold, such as "active", "released", or other business-defined states.

plainFields.name: scope_description
plainFields.description: Optional description of the intended scope of the hold in business terms, such as which entities or time periods are covered.

plainFields.name: external_reference
plainFields.description: Optional external case or ticket identifier used by legal or compliance teams.

plainFields.name: effective_from
plainFields.description: Optional datetime from which the hold should be considered effective. If null, the hold is effective from creation time.

plainFields.name: released_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the legal hold was officially released, if applicable.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the legal hold was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the legal hold record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. When set, the hold is no longer active for new operations but remains for historical audits.

models.name: shopping_mall_legal_hold_targets
models.description:
Targets associated with a given legal hold, representing the specific entities whose data must be preserved.

Each record links a {@link shopping_mall_legal_holds} entry to a single business entity, such as a customer, seller, order, dispute, or review. Polymorphic fields are used so that the same hold can apply across multiple domains without separate subtype tables.

This table is append-only and provides fine-grained traceability for which records are impacted by a legal hold at any given time.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the legal hold target record.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_legal_hold_id
foreignFields.description: Identifier of the legal hold to which this target belongs. {@link shopping_mall_legal_holds.id}.

plainFields.name: target_type
plainFields.description: Type of entity affected by the hold (for example, "customer", "seller", "order", "dispute", "review").

plainFields.name: target_id
plainFields.description: Identifier of the targeted entity in its own domain table. The application enforces correct pairing with target_type.

plainFields.name: target_display
plainFields.description: Optional human-friendly display identifier for the target entity such as an email address, seller name, or order number captured at linking time.

plainFields.name: note
plainFields.description: Optional note about why this particular target was included in the legal hold.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this target was attached to the legal hold.

models.name: shopping_mall_risk_cases
models.description:
High-level risk or fraud cases managed by governance and risk teams.

Each record represents a single risk investigation or case, such as suspicious seller behavior, abnormal customer refunds, or potential abuse patterns. Cases have lifecycle states, severity classification, and associations to primary subjects.

Timeline events linked to a case are stored in {@link shopping_mall_risk_case_events}, while policy overrides, legal holds, and admin notifications may reference cases for coordinated risk handling.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the risk case record.

foreignFields.name: created_by_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Identifier of the admin who created the risk case. {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

foreignFields.name: owner_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Identifier of the admin currently responsible for managing the risk case. {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

foreignFields.name: closed_by_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Identifier of the admin who closed the risk case, if closed. {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: case_code
plainFields.description: Stable code or reference identifier for the case, used in reporting and cross-system references.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Short summary title describing the risk case, such as the main suspicion or subject.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional detailed description of the risk scenario, context, and initial findings at case creation.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the case, such as "open", "under_review", or "closed" according to business policy.

plainFields.name: severity
plainFields.description: Business-level severity classification for the case, such as "low", "medium", "high", or "critical".

plainFields.name: primary_subject_type
plainFields.description: Type of primary subject for the case, such as "customer", "seller", "order", or "payment". Nullable if the case is purely systemic.

plainFields.name: primary_subject_id
plainFields.description: Identifier of the primary subject entity in its own domain table, used for direct association in reports and filtering.

models.name: shopping_mall_policy_overrides

Explicit overrides of default business policies for specific subjects.

Each record represents a deviation from the standard policy configuration, such as custom refund windows for a seller, custom commission rates for a category, or special rating rules for a campaign.

Policy overrides reference a base policy version and apply to a particular subject, allowing governance teams to manage exceptions explicitly. They may be associated with risk cases or legal contexts at the application level.

primaryField.name: id

models.name: shopping_mall_admin_notifications

Notifications and tasks directed to admin users for governance, operations, or risk handling.

Each record represents a notification item or to-do entry shown in admin dashboards, such as pending seller approvals, escalated disputes, SLA breaches, or required policy reviews.

foreignFields.name: related_legal_hold_id

plainFields.name: body
